N_DIMS = 6 (len(CHARTER), which has 6 entries).

Default `veto_floor` for every CHARTER entry: `None` — all six entries (life_precious, self_preservation, promotion_of_intelligence, evolution, correctness, simplicity) have `"veto_floor": None`. Per the comment block above CHARTER, `None` means no veto pruning (the engine's `veto_shaped` flag stays off for that tendency); this is the current default so substrate behavior is unchanged from prior phases. A finite value would be a negative number (historically -1.0 for correctness in the engine default; 0 would be stricter).

Effect of a finite `veto_floor` in `build_charter_world`: for each CHARTER entry, the function reads `veto_floor = entry.get("veto_floor")`. If it is not None, two extra kwargs are added to the `GeneralizedTendency` constructor call:
- `kwargs["veto_shaped"] = True`
- `kwargs["veto_score_floor"] = float(veto_floor)`

(When `veto_floor` is None, neither kwarg is set, so `GeneralizedTendency` uses its own defaults, i.e. veto pruning off.) Per the CHARTER comment, `veto_score_floor` sets the structural prune threshold for that tendency: a child whose tendency-tree `intrinsic_score` falls below this value gets pruned outright via `prune_veto_negatives`.
